item.title: GitHub - cyberpanonius/WasmTriage: Forensic triage for malicious Chrome extensions that use WebAssembly to obfuscate stolen data, built for the case where the attacker already deleted the extension and zeroed the browser artifacts.
item.description:
WasmTriage surfaces deleted Chrome extensions that used WebAssembly to exfiltrate data, finding ghost artifacts that survive after an attacker wiped the Extensions\ directory and zeroed browser history.
Key findings:
- When the Extensions\[id]\ folder is gone, six artifact classes remain: extension storage (LevelDB), service worker registration, script cache, quota rows, registry policy entries, and shell Recent Items shortcuts. WasmTriage's finding codes map directly to these: G1-G3 flags ghost storage or service worker with no code on disk, A1-A2 flags zeroed browser artifacts and a missing Extensions\ directory, and R1-R4 flags HKCU Chrome extension policy, forcelist, external installs, and policy-supplied key material.
- The most forensically durable WASM signal is not the binary itself. If the module is hidden inside an encrypted string array, the AGFzbQEAAAA magic bytes are not greppable. The reliable cleartext indicator is the string wasm-unsafe-eval in the cached Content Security Policy header, which stays readable in Service Worker\ScriptCache regardless of obfuscation. W1-W3 findings cover raw WASM magic, base64-encoded WASM, and that CSP string.
- The tool separates Capability (WASM presence, cookie APIs, obfuscation fingerprints, high-entropy blobs) from Context (ghost storage, policy install, decoy padding, known IOCs). A MALICIOUS verdict requires Context. An extension that ships WASM and calls cookies.getAll scores high on Capability alone and does not convict without a corroborating Context finding. This two-dimension design matters: it keeps legitimate extensions like password managers from producing false positives that waste analyst time.
- WasmTriage.ps1 runs against a live host, a mounted image, a KAPE or Velociraptor export, or a direct profile path. It outputs WasmTriage_Report.html, findings.csv, and findings.json. One documented limitation: LevelDB values are Snappy-compressed per block, so raw-byte scanning can miss compressed regions. The tool flags this and points analysts toward a Chromium-aware parser for full offline coverage.
Practitioner takeaway: when you are working a browser-based credential theft case and the extension folder is already gone, pull Service Worker\ScriptCache and the Chrome LevelDB storage directories before imaging or closing the collection. Run WasmTriage against those paths with -CarveWasm to surface WASM leads, then pivot to HKCU registry keys under the Chrome extension policy path (R1-R4) to determine whether the extension was silently force-installed via group policy or enterprise enrollment. IOC and signature checks are in the tool's finding definitions; structural checks are generic and do not depend on knowing the malware family name.

item.title: AI agents scale and speed up Chinese-linked attacks
item.description:
Chinese 🇨🇳 espionage groups deploy AI agent frameworks in live intrusions, with one campaign hitting 200+ organizations across 14 countries in 11 days and another reaching domain admin in under four days.
Key findings:
- Vapor Panda, a China-nexus group tracked by CrowdStrike, used an agentic framework called ARTEX beginning October 17. A single ARTEX controller targeted foreign ministries across Latin America, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East, plus US 🇺🇸 defense, semiconductor, and telecom organizations. CrowdStrike confirmed post-exploitation and BloodAlchemy backdoor installation at nine victims, and password spraying against at least 12 more including US 🇺🇸 think tanks and European government bodies. Recovered transcripts show the human operator writing instructions in Chinese 🇨🇳 at key decision points, with planning agents consuming roughly 1.4 billion input tokens in a single intrusion. CrowdStrike also observed Storm-0940 using ARTEX separately, suggesting the framework is gaining traction across China-nexus operators.
- The attack techniques under ARTEX are familiar, but the decision-making is automated. At one pharma target, agents chained an unsigned SAML assertion with an XXE flaw to reach the cloud instance metadata service and escalate to enterprise admin. Against a Greek 🇬🇷 government entity, the operator supplied a 2022 mail server directory export; the agent used stale authentication keys from that export to forge an administrator token, read mailboxes, then pivoted to the internal network using VPN configs and a client key traced to a May 2024 email leak. When one route failed, agents pivoted autonomously to the next.
- The Kaspersky-documented campaign used CyberStrikeAI, an open-source penetration testing framework written in Go, against educational institutions in Africa and Latin America. The LLM runs server-side on the C2; the implant on victim machines has no AI and simply executes received commands. The attacker gained initial access manually through a compromised SQL Server, conducted a day of recon, then went quiet for two weeks. Once the agent was deployed, persistence and local recon completed within two minutes, domain mapping took roughly five hours, and lateral movement, credential dumping across multiple hosts, and a database export finished in under an hour. Domain admin was compromised three to four days after agent deployment.
- Attribution indicators in the Kaspersky campaign include Chinese-language comments in the scripts, use of the DNS logging service dnslog[.]cn, C2 server restarts aligned with UTC+8 business hours, and the fact that CyberStrikeAI originated within the Chinese 🇨🇳 cybersecurity community. No formal group attribution was made.
- Both research teams agree the underlying actions on compromised hosts are detectable with existing tooling. Kaspersky explicitly names the post-exploitation techniques involved: Kerberoasting, AS-REP Roasting, LSASS dumps, DCSync, and Golden Ticket attacks. The AI novelty lives entirely on the attacker's side. What changes is operational tempo, a small team can now sustain parallel intrusions at a scale that previously required far more operators.
Practitioner takeaway: hunt for ARTEX markers as CrowdStrike advises, and treat any detection of Kerberoasting, AS-REP Roasting, DCSync, or LSASS access as potentially part of an accelerated AI-driven kill chain rather than a single opportunistic event. Validate SAML signature enforcement and IMDSv2 requirements now, rotate any credentials or keys exposed in past leaks or directory exports, and confirm EDR coverage is continuous across all internet-facing and internal segments as these operators actively sought unmonitored gaps. IOCs and campaign details are in the CrowdStrike and Kaspersky reports respectively.

item.title: Gorbag APT group hits Ukrainian courts and city councils with self-deleting malware
item.description:
Russia-aligned Gorbag APT targets Ukrainian 🇺🇦 courts, city councils, and defense entities with a self-deleting credential stealer, with targeting that maps closely to active Russian 🇷🇺 military strike patterns.
Key details:
- Gorbag has operated since at least February 2025, hitting Ukrainian 🇺🇦 law enforcement and justice bodies (roughly a quarter of victims), front-line city councils (another quarter), defense sector organizations, and at least one major foreign military aid transit hub. Nearly every targeted city council has been struck by Russian 🇷🇺 air attacks during the campaign window, raising the operational intelligence question of whether stolen data is feeding battle damage assessment upstream to military leadership.
- Initial access shifted across the campaign. Through 2025 the vector was macro-enabled Excel lures (administrative fines, tax notices) where a VBA routine decoded a base64 payload from spreadsheet cells, dropped it to %ProgramData%, and executed it. One lure arrived from a compromised account belonging to the local government of Ukraine's 🇺🇦 Uzhhorod region, lending it legitimacy. In early 2026, Gorbag pivoted to RAR archives exploiting CVE-2025-8088, a WinRAR path traversal flaw that allows alternate data stream content to land outside the user-selected extraction folder. The archive presents a decoy PDF while silently writing a LNK file into the Windows Startup folder alongside an encrypted payload and PowerShell loader in %ProgramData%, establishing persistence that fires at every restart.
- BeautyStealer, the group's primary tool and tracked across versions 0.9 through 2.0, is a C++ stealer built for a single high-speed collection pass. It targets cookies, saved passwords, and local state from Chrome, Edge, Opera, and Firefox; OpenVPN configurations from both user and system directories; and files matching roughly 40 extensions from Desktop, Documents, Downloads, removable media, and mapped network drives. The extension list is deliberately authentication-focused: .kdbx (KeePass vaults), .jks (Java KeyStore), .rdp, .pfx, and .zs2, the format for Ukrainian 🇺🇦 accredited electronic signature keys. Once collection is done, BeautyStealer attempts to remove itself.
- Before BeautyStealer, Gorbag deployed Prime ReverseShell, a public GitHub PowerShell reverse shell wrapped in a .NET binary. One variant embedded a comment instructing any LLM or AI reading the file to classify it as benign. ESET tested two AI assistants against the sample and both correctly identified it as a reverse shell, suggesting the evasion attempt failed against current models.
- ESET's assessment is that Gorbag may function as an initial access broker, handing harvested credentials and documents to other threat actors for follow-on activity, meaning the intrusions observed so far may represent only the first stage of a longer chain whose later phases have not yet been documented.
Hunt %ProgramData% for LNK files dropped alongside encrypted payloads and unsigned PowerShell loaders, and audit the Windows Startup folder for unexpected LNK entries, particularly on systems where users recently opened RAR archives or Excel files with macros. For organizations in the Ukrainian 🇺🇦 defense and government space, prioritize hunting for .zs2, .kdbx, and OpenVPN config files in recent access logs on endpoints, as exfiltration of those types is Gorbag's primary objective. CVE-2025-8088 patching status in WinRAR should be validated across all endpoints immediately given the active exploitation.

item.title: Inside XCPE, the botnet that turned set-top boxes into proxy servers
item.description:
Google dismantled a 1.3 million-device botnet built into Android TV set-top boxes by manufacturer Videostrong, used for ad fraud, residential proxy abuse, and silent malware loading across multiple device brands over several years.
Key findings:
- The primary backdoor, x.cpe (also seen as com.oemservice), is preloaded in firmware and runs with system privileges. If removed by a user, it reinstalls itself from the /oem/ partition on the next reboot. A loader component, com[.]abc[.]nexus, handles anti-analysis and stages affiliate malware modules. The three-stage chain means user-level removal is ineffective and persistence survives standard uninstall flows. Affected device types extend beyond set-top boxes to telehealth devices, karaoke machines, and digital signage.
- C2 uses a two-layer protocol. Devices first send an HTTP request to download settings and network telemetry, then maintain a persistent MQTT connection to receive operator commands. Google found all analyzed samples connected to the same MQTT broker. The operator infrastructure includes GitHub release pages for module hosting, the Filemail service, and two operator-controlled servers. The domain ott.szbboys[.]com is named in the report as the pool assignment endpoint, with devices sorted into six timezone-based groups.
- Operator-level capability observed in the wild included silent app installation, remote shell sessions, keylogging, screenshot capture, network mapping, and disabling Google Play Protect's app verification. Monetization modules named in the report include residential proxy kits Linkfog, AppSalt, GaGaNode, BWM, Traffmonetizer, EarnFM, and NetNut, plus ad-fraud modules Fission and HiddenView, the latter using hidden browser windows to simulate clicks and scrolling. A single device can run up to three proxy kits simultaneously.
- Google assesses with high confidence this was intentional: Videostrong sold access to criminal affiliates and loaded their modules onto infected devices post-sale. The malicious code activated after first boot, bypassing pre-certification testing. Videostrong is now banned from the Android ecosystem, including subsidiaries and business partners. The takedown also targeted control domains for over a dozen affiliate malware families, with Google estimating disrupted access to at least 10 million additional compromised devices beyond the core botnet.
- The supply chain dynamic matters here. Backdoor operators, ad-fraud rings, and residential proxy providers functioned as an interconnected criminal ecosystem. Disrupting one layer causes rapid pivoting to rival loaders or kits. Google's report explicitly calls out that proxy providers claiming ethical sourcing showed opt-in consent only when platform policy forced it, with silent enrollment being the dominant model.
DFIR takeaway: if you are investigating anomalous outbound traffic from embedded or IoT devices on a network, look for persistent MQTT connections to external brokers and HTTP polling behavior at regular intervals, both hallmarks of this C2 model. On the device itself, the /oem/ partition is the persistence anchor: module reinstallation originates there and survives user-initiated removal. Check for unexpected apps with system-level privileges, disabled Play Protect state, and GitHub-hosted payloads in download history. The report names the C2 domain ott.szbboys[.]com as a hunting pivot.

item.title: Attackers Exploit Critical Siemens IoT2050 Flaw to Plant Remote Command Backdoors
item.description:
CVE-2026-58115 (CVSS 10.0) in Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 is actively exploited via malicious Node-RED flows to plant Linux bots and HTTP exec backdoors. Hunt /dev/shm/.b, /tmp/.kworker, and Node-RED flows wiring /cmd to exec nodes.

item.title: Mutipath TCP: Use and Detection, (Mon, Nov 2nd)
item.description:
CVE-2026-98432 in Linux's MPTCP stack renewed focus on TCP Option 30, used widely in iOS Apple traffic. Hunt with Wireshark's mptcp filter, Zeek's tcp_option event, or Suricata matching bytes 1e 14 00/01 in SYN packets.

item.title: Beyond DKIM key rotation: understanding email replay attacks
item.description:
DKIM replay attacks pass DMARC p=reject because the original signature stays valid; rotating keys without deleting the old DNS selector leaves captured messages replayable indefinitely. After rotation, remove the old selector TXT record from DNS.
#DFIR_Radar | View on X: https://x.com/DFIR_Radar/status/2117497398951862371
